title: Res and Sat functors between Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ) and Coeff_M⁰(B(M))
body_html:
Restriction and saturation functors $\Res$, $\Sat$

Notation: depth-zero coefficient systems on $\mathcal B(M)$

$\Coeff_M^0(\mathcal B(M))$ denotes the full subcategory of $M$-equivariant coefficient systems $\mathscr W$ on $\mathcal B(M)$ (in the sense of Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ) with axioms (EC1)–(EC4) specialized to $\Phi = (\mathscr K_+, \mathbf 1) = (M_{\bullet, 0+}, \mathbf 1)$) on those $\mathscr W$ such that for every facet $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal B(M)$, the parahoric pro-$p$ radical $M_{\mathcal F, 0+}$ acts trivially on $\mathscr W_\mathcal F$. Equivalently, $\Coeff_M^0(\mathcal B(M))$ is the depth-zero coefficient-system category of [Schneider–Stuhler]; it is the target of the depth-zero localization functor for $M$.

$\mathfrak{R}$ on $\BSigma$

For $\mathscr{V} \in \Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$, define $$\mathfrak{R}\mathscr{V} := (\kappa^* \otimes \mathscr{V})_J, \qquad (\mathfrak{R}\mathscr{V})_\mathcal{F} := (\kappa_\mathcal{F}^* \otimes \mathscr{V}_\mathcal{F})_{J_\mathcal{F}}.$$ The $G$-action on $\mathfrak{R}\mathscr{V}_\mathcal{F}$ sends $T$ to $(g^\mathscr{V}_\mathcal{F}) \circ T \circ (g^\kappa_\mathcal{F})^{-1}$; restrictions are the natural projections.

Restriction $\Res$

By [[node:coefficient_systems.A_over_K_equivalence]], the natural functor $[A/\mathscr{K}_M] \to [A/\mathscr{K}]$ yields $\mathbb{III} : [\mathcal{B}(M)/M] \to [\BSigma / G]$. Set $$\Res(\mathscr{V}) := \mathbb{III}^*(\mathfrak{R}(\mathscr{V})).$$

Lemma. $\Res \mathscr{V}$ defines a coefficient system on $\mathcal{B}(M)$, and moreover $\Res \mathscr{V} \in \Coeff_M^0(\mathcal{B}(M))$.
proof_html:
By (E2), $\mathscr{V}_x|_{M_{x, 0+}}$ is $\kappa_x|_{M_{x, 0+}}$-isotypic, so $M_{x, 0+}$ acts trivially on $(\Res \mathscr{V})_\mathcal{F}$. Transitivity of restrictions follows by direct check.

Saturation $\Sat$

For $\mathscr{W} \in \Coeff_M^0(\mathcal{B}(M))$ and a pair $(g, \mathcal{F})$ with $\mathcal{F}$ in $\mathcal{B}(M)$, define $$\mathscr{V}_{g, \mathcal{F}} := {}^g(\mathscr{W}_\mathcal{F} \otimes \kappa_\mathcal{F}).$$

For another pair $(g', \mathcal{F}')$ with $g \mathcal{F} = g' \mathcal{F}'$, there is $n \in N$ with $n \mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}'$ and a canonical isomorphism $\mathscr{V}_{g, \mathcal{F}} \cong \mathscr{V}_{g', \mathcal{F}'}$ using (K4) (which gives an action of $n^{-1} (g')^{-1} g \in K_\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathscr{W}_\mathcal{F}$ via $\hat K_\mathcal{F}/K_{\mathcal{F}, 0+} \cong \hat M_\mathcal{F}/M_{\mathcal{F}, 0+}$).

For each facet $\mathcal{F}$ in $\BSigma$, set $$(\Sat \mathscr{W})_\mathcal{F} := \varinjlim_{(g, \mathcal{F}')} \mathscr{V}_{g, \mathcal{F}'},$$ where the colimit is over pairs $(g, \mathcal{F}')$ with $g \mathcal{F}' = \mathcal{F}$.

Restrictions are induced from those of $\mathscr{W}$ along a witnessing choice of $(g, \mathcal{F}')$; this is well-defined by the canonical isomorphisms.

Lemma. $\Sat : \Coeff_M^0(\mathcal{B}(M)) \to \Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$ is a functor.
